component.name: Pinto Slicer
component.summary: Prepare, support, slice, and export resin 3D prints

description.p: Pinto Slicer is a Linux-first resin 3D printer slicer built with Rust, egui, and wgpu. It provides a graphical workspace and command-line tools for preparing models and exporting native printer jobs.

ul.li: Move, rotate, scale, mirror, align, and arrange STL and OBJ models
Generate configurable automatic supports with presets
Inspect sliced exposure masks with layer playback
Save self-contained projects with embedded meshes
Export twelve job formats at native printer panel resolutions

description.p: Printer files have software-level validation, but physical-printer interoperability has not been verified. Run a small test print before starting a long job.

screenshot.caption: Automatic support generation on the build plate

description.p: The first public release of Pinto Slicer, with packages for Linux, macOS, and Windows.

ul.li: Interactive model preparation and automatic support generation
Layer preview, project files, and native printer-job export
Linux AppImage and Flatpak, universal macOS DMG, and portable Windows ZIP

description.p: Repeating a piece, and closing the window when it is time.

ul.li: The left strip copies a picked piece as many times as asked for
Mirror puts a mirrored copy beside it, across X, Y or Z
Quitting without saving closes the window again

description.p: Seeing the plate flat, and getting back to the usual angle.

ul.li: Persp and Ortho chips swap the lens under the viewport caption
A house under the orientation cube returns to the three-quarter view

description.p: Finding last week's plate again, and not losing this one.

ul.li: The File menu lists the last ten files that were opened or saved.
Closing the window with unsaved work asks to save, discard or stay.

description.p: Picking the piece you see, after a piece has been removed.

ul.li: Removing a piece rebuilds the drawn plate, so a click and the delete that follows act on the same piece

description.p: The layer playback got its own speed and loop controls.

ul.li: 0.5x, 1x, 2x and 4x speed buttons under the transport
A Loop switch that either starts the plate over at the top layer or stops playback there

description.p: The preset and density rows each own one number again.

ul.li: Presets change only the tip, branch, trunk and foot thicknesses
Density changes only how far apart the tips are; the two rows no longer move each other
The preset row is labelled Strut sizes so it is not mistaken for a density control

description.p: The support density control sits where it can be found, and presets agree with it.

ul.li: The Density row moved to the top Support card, directly under Preset
Presets set the density too: Light 8 mm, Medium 6 mm, Heavy 4 mm
A new plate grows about half as many supports, since the default is now 6 mm between tips

description.p: A density control for automatic supports, and fewer support columns.

ul.li: Low, Medium and High density presets on the Support tab, plus a 1.5-12 mm spacing slider
Tip spacing now sets the actual distance between supports instead of bottoming out on a fixed first-layer radius
Neighbouring tips share one trunk and foot, so a dense run no longer grows a column under every contact

description.p: Responsive slicing feedback and solid cross-sections.

ul.li: Animated working status while supports are generated, the plate is sliced, or a job is exported
Slicing runs in the background instead of freezing the window
Filled 3D cross-sections and no more hollow ball or tube supports
Opening a project no longer generates supports without being asked

description.p: Patch release for support and base geometry in exported jobs.

ul.li: Rebuild project supports automatically when a project is opened
Wait for support generation before exporting, so jobs include the support base and supports
Progressive 3D cross-section that follows the layer slider
Responsive model highlighting with cached picking
Slice-tab 3D/Slices toggle and clearer Values dialog naming

description.p: Patch release for CXDLPv4 export compatibility.

ul.li: Quantize layer height to three decimal places so UVtools accepts the generated job file
3D previews for every support setting, with a translucent model for a clear view
Reset defaults, Prepare-only transform tools, and clearer Slice and Export controls
Faster layer-mask generation and corrected HALOT-X1 CXDLPv4 output
Connected cone, post, and branch geometry, including angled support junctions
Per-model support cleanup after moving, rotating, or deleting models
Uniform scaling by default, with optional independent axis scaling
